characters.name: Miss Mary Sutherland
characters.note: Visitor, typewriter, short-sighted, stepdaughter of James Windibank.

characters.name: James Windibank
characters.note: Stepfather of Mary Sutherland who disguised himself as her fiancé Hosmer Angel.

characters.name: Hosmer Angel
characters.note: Disguise adopted by James Windibank; not a separate person.

characters.name: Mrs. Sutherland
characters.note: Mary's mother, married to James Windibank; complicit in the deception.

characters.name: Mrs. Etherege
characters.note: Former client mentioned only as a referrer.

brief.place: Baker Street lodgings of Sherlock Holmes; a sitting room with a fire, armchairs, a mantelpiece, bottles and test-tubes. Also London streets and a church near King's Cross.
brief.dress: Victorian: Mary Sutherland wears a slate-coloured broad-brimmed straw hat with a brick-red feather, a black jacket with jet beadwork, a brown dress with purple plush at neck and sleeves, grey worn gloves, odd boots, small gold earrings and a fur boa. Windibank is clean-shaven, sallow, in a shiny top-hat; disguised as Hosmer Angel with tinted glasses, bushy black side-whiskers and moustache, black frock-coat, grey Harris tweed trousers, gold Albert chain. Holmes wears a dressing gown and smokes a clay pipe.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Typewriter with worn 'e' and tailless 'r'; typewritten letters and advertisement slip; snuffbox of old gold with amethyst; a hansom cab and four-wheeler; a hunting crop; magnifying lens; hydrochloric acid and test-tubes; the church door.
depiction_rules: Show Mary Sutherland as a short-sighted, good-humoured woman with a large hat, not as a fragile figure.
Depict Windibank in the disguise of Hosmer Angel (tinted glasses, whiskers) when acting as the fiancé, and unmasked in the final confrontation.
Keep the Baker Street room period-accurate with the fire and oil lamps; no modern electric fittings.
Holmes and Watson are shown together in the fireside scenes; Holmes is typically seated, with his feet on the mantelpiece.
